question: If the matrix $A=[a_{ij}]_{2\times2}$ is such that $a_{ij}=\begin{cases}1,&\text{if } i\ne j\\ 0,&\text{if } i=j\end{cases}$ then $A+A^{2}$ is equal to:
explanation:
**Step 1:** Construct matrix $A$ from its definition requirements: diagonal elements $a_{11}=a_{22}=0$ and off-diagonal elements $a_{12}=a_{21}=1$, yielding $A = \begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 2:** Compute $A^2$ using matrix multiplication: $\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 3:** Perform addition: $A + A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$, which corresponds to Option C.
